messages:
alisha: Heads-up — we're seeing a thundering herd of tiny GPU pods (0.125-0.5 GPU) landing on a few nodes in us-west1-rack2. Large gang jobs keep getting evicted or starved. Any ideas?

matt: saw that spike in metrics at ~03:10. node GPU_util low but free slots fragmented. scheduler keeps packing tiny pods into leftovers.

jin: can you paste a quick `kubectl get pods`/eviction sample?

alisha: pasted below from the node: 
```
NAME                                     READY   STATUS    NODE                CPU  GPU
train-large-0                            1/1     Running   node-gpu-3         8    2
small-experiment-abc                     1/1     Running   node-gpu-3         0.1  0.125
small-experiment-def                     1/1     Evicted   node-gpu-3         0.1  0.125
tiny-batch-xyz                           0/1     Evicted   node-gpu-3         0.05 0.125
```

diego: ugh. that's classic mini-gang pocketing — lots of tiny allocations fragmenting GPU capacity so big pods can't get contiguous GPUs.

kira: quick mitigation: taint a small-pool nodeclass and add toleration only for known small workloads. then drain/cordon the hot nodes.

matt: agree. alternative is to enforce a `LimitRange` that sets minimum GPU request increments (e.g., 0.5) for general namespace so tiny pods get scheduled to a small pool instead.

jin: descheduler/compaction job might help reclaim leftovers periodically. but that can cause churn.

alisha: thinking of a 3-step plan: 1) label + taint three nodes as `small-gpu=true` and create nodeSelector for low-priority tiny jobs, 2) run a descheduler compaction cron to consolidate small pods nightly, 3) add admission webhook to tag tiny pods to the small pool. anyone opposed?

diego: +1, but we need rollout plan for canary so we don't push critical infra tests into tiny pool by accident. also set eviction threshold higher for large jobs.

kira: sample toleration/taint snippet for reference: 
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: tiny-batch
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "small-gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeSelector:
    nodeclass: small-gpu
  resources:
    limits:
      nvidia.com/gpu: 0.125
```

matt: also consider a scheduler plugin to prefer packing small pods into packed islands (compact binpack) instead of scattering. but that's more infra work.

sre-bot: ALERT: GPU fragmentation anomaly detected in us-west1 at 2026-03-20T03:12:05Z — fragmentation index = 0.78 (+0.32 vs baseline)

alisha: thanks. i'll open a short runbook and start the taint/label change in staging first. can someone pair for the admission webhook? @jin?

jin: can do. i'll sketch the mutating webhook today.

diego: i'll prepare a small-pool nodegroup terraform change and a drain plan for canary.

kira: i'll create a dashboard panel showing contiguous GPU availability (per-node max contiguous block) so we can watch effect.

alisha: plan posted in #eng-platform-ops-docs after canary. TL;DR: create small-pool, route tiny jobs there, descheduler compaction nightly, monitor. :thumbsup:

matt: sounds good. follow-up: let's also audit CI/cron jobs that request tiny GPUs and mark which can be batched together.

alisha: agreed — will add that to the runbook. thanks all.
